articles.titulo: Metabolite-Driven Immunometabolic Crosstalk in Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: The Macrophage-Disc Cell Interface.
articles.autores: Ma D, Zhao J, … Ma T (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is accompanied by extracellular-matrix disruption, metabolic stress and immune-cell infiltration, but how metabolites mediate communication between disc cells and macrophages remains incompletely defined. This narrative review examines lactate, succinate and kynurenine as candidate signalling metabolites at the macrophage-disc cell interface and proposes an integrative metabolite-centred framework. Evidence is strongest for lactate, which is supported by IVDD-specific studies linking glycolytic adaptation and impaired clearance to acidosis, MCT-dependent metabolic coupling, ASIC/NLRP3 activation, lactylation, cellular senescence and matrix catabolism. Evidence for succinate is more limited: IVDD-specific studies support SIRT5-AIFM1-dependent succinylation and mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas succinate accumulation and SUCNR1-mediated macrophage signalling in human degenerative discs remain unverified. The kynurenine-AhR axis is primarily hypothesis-generating; emerging IVDD-related observations implicate AhR and tryptophan-pathway changes, but a causal kynurenine-AhR macrophage-disc pathway has not been established. We propose that degenerating disc cells may reprogramme the local metabolic microenvironment, thereby altering macrophage functional states and creating a self-amplifying immunometabolic loop that feeds back on disc-cell injury and extracellular-matrix degradation. Future studies should combine spatial immunometabolomics in human tissue with cell-specific and causal intervention experiments to distinguish established mechanisms from context-dependent or extrapolated pathways and to evaluate potential microenvironment-directed therapeutic targets.

articles.titulo: Gut microbiota-host co-metabolism in sepsis and critical illness: source, compartment, immune state, and host defense.
articles.autores: Wu C, Liu R (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Critical illness can profoundly disturb the intestinal microbiota-metabolite-host immune axis through the combined effects of shock, hypoxia, altered nutritional intake, antimicrobial exposure, organ dysfunction, and impaired epithelial barrier integrity. These changes can reshape microbial metabolic capacity, host co-metabolism, and systemic metabolite exposure, while the host may simultaneously exhibit overlapping features of hyperinflammation, immune tolerance, lymphocyte dysfunction, impaired antimicrobial defense, and tissue repair. Metabolites generated through microbial metabolism or shared microbial-host pathways may therefore contribute to immune reprogramming, although their effects are highly context dependent and cannot be regarded as uniformly beneficial or detrimental. This narrative review examines short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived indoles, secondary bile acids, succinate, lactate, trimethylamine N-oxide, polyamines, and aromatic metabolites, with particular attention to source attribution, anatomical compartment, host co-metabolism, receptor signaling, and their potential influence on antimicrobial immunity. These metabolites may act through G-protein-coupled receptors, AhR, PXR, FXR, TGR5, VDR, HIF-1α, inflammasome pathways, mitochondrial signaling, and epigenetic mechanisms to modulate macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells, innate lymphoid cells, T lymphocytes, epithelial barriers, and endothelial responses. The direction and magnitude of these effects are likely to vary according to timing, concentration, anatomical compartment, immune-cell state, pathogen burden, and renal or hepatic clearance. Within this framework, attenuation of inflammatory signaling may help limit early collateral tissue injury, yet the same response could become disadvantageous when antimicrobial competence is already impaired. Similarly, succinate and lactate may reflect or contribute to distinct inflammatory, regulatory, or reparative programs depending on whether they arise from microbial or host metabolism and whether they act within intracellular or extracellular compartments. Human studies in critically ill populations have linked dysbiosis and metabolomic alterations with secondary infection, prolonged organ support, and mortality; however, most have not been able to resolve microbial source attribution or establish causal mediation. Future work would therefore benefit from integrating longitudinal microbiome, metabolome, immune-function, and organ-clearance measurements with source-resolved approaches, including isotope tracing, as well as state-specific and trajectory-informed clinical endpoints. Microbiome-directed interventions may be most appropriately investigated as context-dependent modulators of host defense rather than as broadly anti-inflammatory strategies.

v6.resumo: Revisão narrativa sobre metabólitos da microbiota intestinal na sepse (ácidos graxos de cadeia curta, indóis, ácidos biliares secundários, succinato, lactato) e seu efeito sobre macrófagos, neutrófilos e linfócitos, por receptores acoplados à proteína G, HIF-1α, inflamassoma, sinalização mitocondrial e mecanismos epigenéticos; os efeitos dependem de tempo, concentração e compartimento.

articles.titulo: Microbiota-mediated blocking ofsporozoites in: a systematic review.
articles.autores: Olafusi CO, Tebamifor ME, … Ogunlana OO (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in the mosquito, Anopheles, is essential for malaria transmission. Despite the unsurprising fact that the mosquito microbiota has become a major factor in the modulation of the competence of mosquitoes, the specific types of microbial taxa and mechanisms affecting the development of the sporozoite are not well synthesized. This systematic review brings together and critically evaluates the available evidence to understand the role of microbiota in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes with a specific focus on the salivary gland microbiome.
A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases (2000-2026) was conducted, and 41 studies met the inclusion criteria. Extraction and synthesis of data were conducted in the form of a narrative in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE's tool for animal studies.
The Wolbachia effects varied by strain and species: wAlbB caused a 3.4- to 3.7-fold decrease in sporozoites, wAnga-Mali had a negative correlation with 95% presence, and there was no correlation for wAnmo in An. moucheti. All African countries (1-57% prevalence) were consistently affected by Microsporidia MB, with no fitness costs. Serratia ureilytica Su_YN1 inhibited ~98% of parasites using outer membrane vesicles loaded with AmLip, which targets parasites via the phosphatidylcholine scavenging pathway. 93% transmission blocking was obtained in mouse models with engineered symbionts (transgenesis + paratransgenesis).
The mosquito microbiota plays a significant, but strain-, species-, and context-dependent role in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites. The Microsporidia and Serratia species are promising candidates for field deployment, offering sustainable, environmentally friendly complements to chemical insecticides for malaria vector control.

v6.implicacao: Malária / Plasmodium (glândula salivar e esporozoíto): a revisão trata o microbioma da glândula salivar como variável da carga de esporozoítos, o que pede registrar a microbiota da colônia de An. darlingi ao medir esporozoítos e procurar bactérias nos cortes de MET de volume de glândula salivar.
v6.resumo: Revisão sistemática (PRISMA, 41 estudos de 2000–2026, risco de viés pelo SYRCLE) sobre como a microbiota do mosquito afeta o desenvolvimento do esporozoíto, com foco no microbioma da glândula salivar. O efeito depende de cepa, espécie e contexto: wAlbB reduziu esporozoítos 3,4 a 3,7 vezes; a cepa bacteriana Su_YN1 inibiu cerca de 98% dos parasitos com vesículas de membrana externa carregadas com AmLip, que atinge a via de captação de fosfatidilcolina do parasito; simbiontes modificados deram 93% de bloqueio de transmissão em camundongo.
v6.metodo: Contagem de esporozoítos em glândula salivar após colonização ou transinfecção com simbionte e ensaio de bloqueio de transmissão em camundongo, os desenhos que a revisão consolida (lido a partir do resumo).

articles.titulo: Integrated Plasmodium falciparum Transcriptomics Reveals Coordinated Stress Adaptation and Metabolic Remodeling in Severe Malarial Anemia.
articles.autores: Perkins D, Onyango C, … Cheng Q (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a leading cause of childhood morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, with severe malarial anemia (SMA; hemoglobin (Hb) < 6.0 g/dL) representing one of the life-threatening complications of Plasmodium falciparum infection. While limited studies have examined host transcriptional responses in SMA, parasite transcriptional adaptations remain unexplored. Here, we performed parasite transcriptomic profiling in the same cohort of Kenyan children under five years of age in whom we previously characterized host transcriptional responses to SMA, including children presenting with SMA (n = 20) or non-SMA malaria (n = 40). Differential expression analysis identified 566 P. falciparum genes associated with SMA, predominantly involving up-regulated transcripts linked to proteostasis, translational regulation, stress-response pathways, and metabolic remodeling. Transcriptomic deconvolution indicated greater trophozoite and schizont representation in SMA, with reduced ring-stage and gametocyte signatures. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and protein-protein interaction network analysis identified coordinated transcriptional programs enriched for proteasomal degradation, ubiquitin-mediated protein turnover, chaperone activity, RNA processing, and metabolic adaptation. XGBoost-SHAP modeling identified a small subset of parasite genes that captured much of the transcriptomic signal, classifying SMA from non-SMA malaria. Collectively, these findings define a distinct parasite transcriptional landscape in SMA characterized by coordinated stress adaptation and metabolic flexibility, highlighting proteostasis-associated pathways for further therapeutic investigation.

v6.resumo: Preprint (Research Square) de transcriptômica integrada de P. falciparum na anemia malárica grave (hemoglobina abaixo de 6,0 g/dL), que descreve adaptação coordenada ao estresse e remodelamento metabólico.

articles.titulo: Evaluation of adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription of artemisinin combination therapy (ACTs) and artesunate in Kilifi County, Kenya.
articles.autores: Ngala JC (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria is a vector-borne disease caused by a protozoan parasite in the genus Plasmodium. The parasite is transmitted by female mosquitoes in the genus Anopheles. The disease is common within the tropics, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. The major early clinical features are fever accompanied by headache, joint pains, malaise, vomiting, and diarrhoea. These symptoms are some instances used as a diagnosis for malaria infection without confirmatory laboratory tests; followed by prescription of first-line antimalarials, mainly artemisinin combination therapy (ACTs). This trend of prescribing antimalarials to patients presenting with malaria-like symptoms without confirmatory laboratory tests is contrary to World Health Organization's (WHO) recommended guidelines. Such practices pose a great risk for suboptimal medication, development of resistance against the drugs, treatment failure, and increased morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this study was conducted to evaluate adherence to WHO-recommended guidelines for prescription of ACTs and artesunate.
This was a cross-sectional study in four health facilities in Kilifi County for a period of one year. 9,940 participants consented to inclusion in the survey. Pre- and post-ACTs/artesunate prescription data was captured using standardized case record forms.
Out of the 9,940 patients, 80.4% had confirmed malaria infections, out of which 60% (n = 4,795) were males. 48% (n = 3,836), of the malaria cases were from rural areas. 17% (n = 1,359), of the positive cases were severe malaria, with 92% (n = 1,251), being in children under the age of 15 years old. Adherence to WHO guidelines for diagnosis of malaria was, at 99% (9,841/9,940), with Rapid diagnostic test as the most used technique, at 74% (n = 7,356). Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription of ACTs was, at 48% (3,184/6,633), with Coartem as the most prescribed ACT, at 98% (n = 6,436). Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription and administration of artesunate was, at 82% (1,114/1,359). Artesunate injection was administered to all cases of severe malaria.
Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription of ACTs and artesunate in Kilifi County had improved substantially, although there exists a room for improvement, especially on instructions on how to take the ACT medications following hospital discharge. Therefore, stakeholders, especially the county's ministry of health, should put more effort into further improvement through seminars, short training courses, and workshops to reduce the disease burden and prevent the likelihood of the development of ACTs and artesunate resistance by malaria parasites in the region.

articles.titulo: Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Differential Exon Usage and Virulence Gene Family Dynamics in Plasmodium falciparum during Severe Malaria
articles.autores: Ansah PM, Dzadey WO, … Awuku W (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a leading cause of child mortality in developing countries, with roughly 610,000 deaths per year. While the disease is caused by five human Plasmodium species, Plasmodium falciparum (Pf ) causes the most severe form. Progression from uncomplicated to severe malaria is characterized by high proliferation of the parasite, severely affecting children under five years old. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression remain an active area of research. Many multicopy genes have been implicated in Pf virulence. Some of these genes are implicated in cytoadherence, host-cell invasion, immune evasion, sequestration of infected erythrocytes, and antigenic variation. We employed an integrative transcriptomic analysis in this study to elucidate the molecular underpinnings of severe malaria and gene expression patterns, virulence gene dynamics, and the potential contribution of alternative splicing. Results show an overexpression of protein synthesis and ribosomal genes associated with severe malaria. About 86% (n=1865) of all differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were downregulated in severe malaria, and 226 genes exhibited both differential expression and differential exon usage (DEU). Pf virulence genes and antigenic genes such as var (pfEMP1), stevor, surfin, rif (rifin), ptm-2TM, and msp were upregulated in severe malaria compared with uncomplicated malaria, except for rifin. In severe malaria, there was evidence of co-expression and regulation within multigene families, as well as DEU and alternative splicing in virulence genes and antimalarial resistance-related proteins. Pf does not employ a single mechanism for disease progression but suppresses and deregulates nonessential pathways, processes, and genes, which are upregulated virulence genes, DNA replication, mRNA transcription, and protein synthesis. Multicopy genes are co-expressed and regulated to meet the molecular needs of the parasite. The parasite employs alternative splicing and DEU mechanisms for immune invasion and evasion, host-parasite interaction, as well as antimalarial resistance.

v6.resumo: Preprint de transcriptômica integrada de P. falciparum na malária grave, com uso diferencial de éxons e dinâmica de famílias gênicas de virulência (resumo lido só no início).

articles.titulo: Therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine plus primaquine in the treatment of uncomplicatedin Shecha Health Center, South Ethiopia.
articles.autores: Dugassa D, Gamachu B, … Brhane BG (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria is one of vector-borne diseases caused by plasmodium species. Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax have a higher prevalence in Ethiopia. To combat this illness, effective therapy is necessary. Chloroquine plus radical cure with 14 days primaquine is a first-line antimalarial treatment for P.vivax. However, malaria treatment in Ethiopia is significantly impeded by resistance. The purpose of this study was to determine the therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine with radical cure with 14 days of primaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated P. vivax in Shecha Health Center, South Ethiopia.
A single-arm, prospective therapeutic efficacy trial was conducted from December 2022 to March 2023 at Shecha Health Center in south Ethiopia. The study subjects were chosen using the purposive sampling technique. The study patients were given a 25 mg/kg standard dosage of chloroquine for three days and a 0.25 mg/kg standard dose of Primaquine for fourteen days. The World Health Organization double-entry Excel sheet was utilized for Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and the laboratory and clinical data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version-26 software. P-values less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The study endpoint was adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 42.
Out of the 100 study participants, 90 (90.0%) completed the 42-day follow-up period. Male research participants make 57 (57%) of the total. Adults made up the majority of the study subjects 60 (60.0%). The adequate clinical and parasitological response rate was 96.7% (95% CI: 90.1-98.9%). On day three, parasitemia was cleared at 80 (82.5%) and fever at 95 (97.9%). There were no serious adverse reactions reported.
Chloroquine plus primaquine is still an effective drug therapy for uncomplicated P.vivax, with rapid clearance of parasitemia, fever, improvement of hemoglobin, and clinical resolution. Therefore, chloroquine plus primaquine should continue as a first-line drug to treat uncomplicated P.vivax malaria in the study area.

articles.titulo: The role of Plasmodium falciparum acyl-coenzyme A synthetase 10 in fatty acid acquisition and lipid synthesis
articles.autores: Fike KR, Santos H, … Klemba M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: During the asexual blood stage, malaria parasites synthesize large quantities of lipids to support their rapid proliferation. Exogenous fatty acids obtained from host plasma are activated for lipid synthesis by parasite acyl-coenzyme A synthetases (ACSs). Of the twelve Plasmodium falciparum ACS homologs, ACS10 has emerged as a key blood-stage enzyme. Here, we sought to define the role of ACS10 in fatty acid acquisition and lipid synthesis during asexual development. To accomplish this, we have employed fatty acid alkyne probes of parasite lipid synthesis together with selective depletion of ACS10 in a conditional knockdown parasite line. This approach revealed that ACS10 is required for efficient incorporation of 16- to 20-carbon unsaturated fatty acid alkynes and a 20-carbon, saturated fatty acid alkyne into the major parasite phospholipids and neutral lipids. In contrast, shorter saturated fatty acid alkynes were either unaffected by ACS10 depletion or were hyper-incorporated into parasite lipids. ACS10 knockdown elicited a profound deformation of the food vacuole, which was likely caused by an imbalance of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids in parasite lipids. To promote the discovery and characterization of ACS inhibitors, we have established a fatty acid alkyne-based approach for identifying compounds that target ACS10 as their primary mode of action.

articles.titulo: Experimental investigation of the relationship between pore structure and methane adsorption in coals with adsorption constant quantification.
articles.autores: Liu J, He S, … Xu H (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The pore system of coal provides both methane storage sites and migration pathways, controlling coalbed methane (CBM) recovery. In this study, five coal samples ranging from bituminous coal to anthracite were investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), low-temperature nitrogen adsorption (LTN2GA), and methane adsorption experiments. The relationships among pore structure parameters, fractal dimension, and methane adsorption behavior were analyzed, and the errors associated with two modified linear methods for calculating Langmuir adsorption constants were evaluated. The results show that highly metamorphosed coals are dominated by micropores and possess larger specific surface areas (SSA). EDS analysis showed that C and O were the dominant elements in the coal samples, accompanied by minor amounts of Al, Si, and S. The fractal dimension exhibits an asymmetric U-shaped trend with decreasing coal rank, and SSA shows an exponential relationship with fractal dimension, particularly within the SSA range of 0-10 m2 g-1. Methane adsorption capacity and adsorption constants increase with decreasing pore size, while pore volume shows no clear correlation with adsorption parameters. Fractal dimension exhibits a positive correlation with adsorption constants, indicating the influence of pore heterogeneity on methane adsorption. The relative errors of adsorption constant a calculated by the two linear methods are 0.08-3.57% and 0.22-1.46%, respectively, while those of b are 0-12.68% and 1.87-16.03%, respectively. The comparison shows that Langmuir parameter estimates depend on the fitting formulation and supports fitting on the original adsorption scale with an appropriate residual model. Although pore characteristics are affected by coal-specific geological conditions, this study provides a useful reference for understanding pore structure-adsorption relationships and CBM reservoir evaluation.

articles.titulo: Leave-One-Out-Cross-Validation Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Efficient, Scalable, and Robust Prediction of Artemisinin Resistance in Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 mutants.
articles.autores: Das R, Dutta S, … Bhattacharjee S (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Emerging Plasmodium falciparum resistance to frontline artemisinin (ART) derivatives threatens global malaria control efforts. Current protocols assigning ART-sensitive (ART-S) or -resistant (ART-R) phenotypes to parasite strains with Kelch13 (K13) mutations remain time-intensive for real-time surveillance. Ring-survival assay (RSA), an ex vivo gold standard mandates laboratory-adaptation under culture conditions and frequently does not replicate clinical ART-responsiveness, thereby limiting its utility for rapidly triaging newly emerging K13 variants. In contrast, advent of artificial intelligence (AI)-derived models hold potential to screen >100 K13 variants within hours, enabling rapid near-real-time prediction of ART-S/R. Here, we engineered a panel of forty representative K13 variants by computing their relative deviations from wild-type K13 across ten physicochemical and structural descriptors, yielding a compact feature set which captures mutation-induced perturbations in folding, stability, and solvent exposure. These can be further utilized to train and validate AI classifier to predict resistance.

articles.titulo: C3a-C3aR Signaling Modulates Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Formation and Contributes to Blood-Brain Barrier Injury After Stroke.
articles.autores: Zhang Q, Xu F, … Duan M (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Stroke causes severe neurological damage, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, complement activation, and neutrophil infiltration. How complement signaling interacts with infiltrating neutrophils in BBB dysfunction remains unclear.
This study aims to elucidate how the C3a-C3aR axis modulates neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and thereby contributes to BBB disruption following stroke.
A transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) rat model was used to induce ischemic stroke. Neurological function, infarct volume, and BBB integrity were assessed using behavioral tests, TTC staining, electron microscopy, and BBB permeability assays. Molecular and histological analyses, including RNA sequencing, immunostaining, HE staining, Nissl staining, ELISA, RT-qPCR, Co-IP, and western blotting, were performed to evaluate complement activation, NETs, and inflammatory responses. The C3a-C3aR axis and NETs formation were pharmacologically modulated to determine their roles in post-stroke BBB damage.
BBB damage, neutrophil infiltration, and neurobehavioral deficits are prominent after stroke. On the third day after the stroke, BBB damage is most pronounced. RNA sequencing revealed that inflammatory responses, complement activation, and NETs formation were identified as central mechanisms. Key driver analysis confirmed that C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with neutrophil responses and NETs formation. Increased numbers of neutrophils infiltrated the brain parenchyma and formed NETs after stroke, in association with BBB damage and neurological injury. C3aR was expressed in neutrophils, consistent with a potential role of C3a-C3aR signaling in neutrophil responses. Inhibiting NETs formation mitigated these poor functional outcomes, ameliorating BBB dysfunction. C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with NETs formation and BBB disruption and neurological injury. Suppression of C3a-C3aR signaling reduced NETs formation and was associated with attenuated BBB disruption and neurological impairment. Conversely, activation of C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with increased NETs formation, BBB disruption, and neurological damage.
Thus, our results indicate that C3a-C3aR signaling is associated with NETs formation, BBB damage, and neurological impairment after stroke and may represent a potential target for further investigation.

articles.titulo: Reconstructing Dengue Exposure Dynamics and Assessing the Public Health Impact of Vaccination Scenarios Using Mathematical Models in Brazil.
articles.autores: Ko Y, Santos CD, … Ko AI (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Brazil experienced its worst dengue epidemic in 2024, with an increase in severe outcomes among elderly individuals, highlighting the need for vaccination strategies informed by population immunity. We reconstructed state- and age-specific immune profiles by fitting an age-structured catalytic model to dengue surveillance data from 2000-2025. This inferred immune profile was incorporated into an SIR-type transmission model to project disease burden and to evaluate the public health impact of vaccine allocation strategies. We observed substantial spatial heterogeneity in accumulated immunity, which was closely associated with projected burden and optimal allocation. Strategies prioritizing states with lower historical incidence and larger susceptible populations yielded greater benefits. Under limited vaccine supply, targeting children resulted in the greatest reductions in DALYs, whereas targeting elderly populations achieved smaller DALY reductions but larger reductions in mortality. We further showed that accelerated vaccine supply markedly increased impact, while allocation choices remained critical when availability was constrained.

articles.titulo: Durability of Yorkoollong-lasting insecticidal nets in Benin: temporal evolution of deltamethrin concentration assessed using portable C-Vue HPLC chromatography during household use.
articles.autores: Hougbe SZ, Ossé RA, … Akogbeto M (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The effectiveness of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) depends on both chemical durability and sustained biological efficacy under operational conditions. However, insecticide depletion over time does not always correspond directly to loss of entomological effectiveness. This study assessed the relationship between deltamethrin content and biological efficacy of Yorkool® LLINs over 18 months of household use in Benin.
A longitudinal study was conducted in southern Benin to monitor Yorkool® LLINs at baseline (T0), 7 months (T7), 12 months (T12), and 18 months (T18). Household practice data were collected and analyzed at all time points except T0. However, chemical and biological evaluations were performed only at T0, T12, and T18. Deltamethrin surface concentrations were quantified using a portable C-Vue HPLC device and expressed in mg/m2. Biological efficacy was assessed using WHO cone bioassays with susceptible Anopheles gambiae Kisumu mosquitoes, measuring knock-down at 60 min and mortality at 24 h. Chemical and biological trends were analyzed comparatively.
Mean deltamethrin concentration declined progressively from approximately 55 mg/m2 at T0 to 50.7 mg/m2 at T12 and 45.3 mg/m2 at T18. Despite this chemical depletion, cone bioassays showed consistently high knock-down and mortality rates, with most nets meeting WHO criteria for optimal or minimal effectiveness. The relationship between insecticide concentration and mosquito mortality was positive but non-linear, suggesting a biological threshold effect.
Yorkool® LLINs maintained high biological efficacy during the first 18 months of use despite moderate chemical depletion. These findings suggest that loss of insecticide content does not immediately translate into loss of functional performance. However, the absence of follow-up up to 36 months and the use of a susceptible mosquito strain limit extrapolation to full operational lifespan and resistance settings. Extended durability studies are needed to define the functional failure threshold of LLINs.

articles.titulo: Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling of childhood anemia in Tanzania: spatial distribution, determinants, and causal impact of malaria.
articles.autores: Njotto LL, Senyoni W, … Lutambi AM (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Childhood anemia remains a major public health challenge in low- and middle income countries, impairing growth, cognition, and child survival. In Tanzania, the burden remains persistently high, yet its spatial patterns, temporal trends, and links to infectious diseases, particularly malaria, are not well understood.
Using four rounds of the Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey (2007/08-2022) and a Bayesian spatio-temporal geostatistical framework with survey-weighted causal inference, we mapped anemia prevalence and quantified the impact of malaria through estimates of average causal effects (ACE), attributable fractions (AF), and numbers needed to treat (NNT).
Anemia prevalence remained high (60.1% overall), with persistent clusters in the western, southern, and Lake Zone areas; prevalence declined from 2007/08 to 2015/16 before rising again in 2022. Malaria emerged as the strongest predictor of anemia, and its effect strengthened with child age: the odds ratio increased from 2.89 (95% CrI: 2.25-3.72) among children aged 6-23 months to 4.07 (3.53-4.71) among those aged 42-59 months. The ACE of malaria peaked at 0.266 in 2015/16, with an AF of 6.4% and the lowest NNT (3.93) recorded in the same year, indicating malaria prevention was most efficient during this period. Minimum temperature above approximately 18°C was associated with increased anemia risk, while precipitation showed no credible association once malaria status was already accounted for; anemia risk was lower at mid-range cluster altitudes (~1,000-1,600 m), consistent with reduced malaria transmission at these elevations. Lower maternal education, household poverty, larger household size, and younger maternal age were also associated with higher anemia risk.
These findings indicate that childhood anemia in Tanzania is driven by entrenched spatial heterogeneity and a strong, age-dependent, time-varying causal relationship with malaria, highlighting the need for geographically targeted, multisectoral strategies that integrate malaria control with broader social, economic, and environmental interventions.

articles.titulo: Preparedness for Imported Malaria in Non-Endemic Europe: Healthcare Workforce Knowledge and Travel-History Practice in Poland.
articles.revista: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.autores: Bogacka A, Grzybek J, … Grzybek M (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Imported malaria remains a diagnostic challenge in non-endemic countries, where timely recognition depends on healthcare workers eliciting recent travel history and initiating appropriate testing. We assessed malaria knowledge, training exposure and self-reported travel-history practice across healthcare worker roles at two reference centres in northern Poland.
We conducted an online cross-sectional survey between October 2023 and April 2024 among doctors, nurses, paramedics and allied healthcare personnel. A 25-item instrument covered aetiology, transmission, prevention, pharmacology, diagnosis and epidemiology. Knowledge scores were compared using non-parametric tests. Regression models exploring sociodemographic and occupational predictors were unstable because few respondents scored highly and are reported as supplementary sensitivity analyses.
Among 402 respondents, the mean knowledge score was 7.4 of 25 (29.6%); 91.3% scored below the predefined threshold and no respondent exceeded 64%. Knowledge gaps were greatest for complete transmission routes (4.0% correct), prevention measures (8.7%), diagnostic methods (12.7%) and contemporary pharmacology. Only 14.4% of doctors reported always asking febrile patients about travel to malaria-endemic regions. Malaria exposure in training was limited: 22.1% recalled coverage in parasitology classes and 3.5% had attended relevant symposia or conferences. No sociodemographic or occupational factor was independently associated with knowledge in any model specification.
Preparedness for imported malaria was weak across this non-endemic healthcare workforce. Strengthening case detection requires routine travel-history prompts in febrile-patient assessment, targeted continuing education and structured coverage of imported tropical infections in pre-graduate curricula.

articles.titulo: Knowledge About Canine Visceral Leishmaniasis in the Municipality of Girón, Santander, Colombia.
articles.autores: Blanco YAC, Ordoñez KDC, … da Rocha CMBM (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study evaluated the perception of the population in the municipality of Girón, Santander, Colombia, regarding knowledge of canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL). A semi-structured survey was conducted with 387 individuals in 2023, to assess their understanding of CVL in Girón, a municipality within the metropolitan area of Bucaramanga, Santander. A descriptive analysis was carried out using JASP software, and associations were tested using the Chi-square and Cramer's V tests, with a significant level of p < 0.05. Only 9.3% of participants had heard of the disease and identified it as zoonotic, while 7.8% reported knowing its mode of transmission. Regarding the vector, 51.2% correctly identified phlebotomine sandflies, although misconceptions persisted-32.6% attributed transmission to Aedes aegypti and 9.3% to dogs. In terms of risk perception, 41.9% believed anyone could suffer from the disease, and 60.5% considered that certain groups were at greater risk. However, only 12.4% recognized CVL as a serious illness, and 8.5% believed it could be fatal. Concerning prevention, 45.0% thought that hygiene could help control the disease, but most did not associate this with veterinary health monitoring. Among respondents with dogs, only 5.6% had ever conducted diagnostic tests, all of which were positive. Considering the significance of CVL as a neglected zoonotic disease and public health problem, this study highlights the limited and inconsistent knowledge of the community. The findings emphasize the need for eco-epidemiological surveillance and educational programs targeting dog owners and veterinarians to strengthen control and prevention strategies for leishmaniasis.

articles.titulo: Emulsion polymerizations stabilized by amphiphilic block-random copolymers in a tubular microreactor with online dynamic light scattering.
articles.autores: Smeltzer SE, Weerarathna LJ, … Cunningham MF (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: A flow setup with a tubular reactor and online dynamic light scattering (DLS) was constructed to study the kinetics of styrene emulsion polymerizations stabilized by polystyrene-b-poly[styrene-r-(acrylic acid)]. Aside from online particle size measurements with DLS, samples were taken for offline gravimetric and molecular weight analysis. All flow data was compared to that obtained in a batch reactor. By varying the volume of the reactor, the polymerization could be monitored from the nucleation period through the particle growth phase, to conversions >90%. The use of the flow system enabled collection of much more detailed particle size data during the seeded-coagulative nucleation period than is possible in batch, however, some notable differences were observed in the flow system. High conversions were enabled by an unexpected and significant enhancement in the rate of polymerization in the flow system compared to batch. The enhancement in the rate of polymerization is postulated to be connected to differences in the entry rate of radicals in the emulsion polymerization process. Electron microscopy images showed multiple populations of particles for high conversion samples from the flow setup, which has been attributed to a population of particles that did not participate in growth due to the unexpectedly high rate of polymerization. The experimental data obtained in this study will form the basis of further modelling studies on the seeded-coagulative nucleation mechanism.

articles.titulo: Leveraging Deep Learning to Reveal Fine-Scale In Vivo Mitochondrial Dynamics and Axonal Transport.
articles.revista: The Yale journal of biology and medicine
articles.autores: Park JY, Chae M, … Sung H (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In axons, mitochondrial transport is essential for neuronal function and survival, and its disruption is increasingly recognized as an early pathological hallmark in multiple neurodegenerative diseases. Despite its importance, quantitative analysis of mitochondrial transport dynamics remains challenging due to complex and heterogeneous motility patterns and reliance on labor-intensive manual tracking methods. Here, we present a deep learning-assisted framework for semiautomated quantification of mitochondrial axonal transport. Using time-lapse confocal imaging of individual in vivo axons in the well-established Drosophila nervous system, we comprehensively validated transport parameters, including displacement and velocity. We further assessed the fidelity of our method in recapitulating expert-derived measurements and its potential to overcome the limitations of conventional manual tracking. Notably, our framework enables detailed characterization of dynamic behaviors during transport, including intensity-based variations and concurrent morphological changes within individual mitochondria, potentially reflecting mitochondrial physiological states that were difficult to resolve with traditional approaches. Collectively, our study establishes the feasibility of next-generation analysis for axonal transport and highlights its potential to uncover previously inaccessible aspects of mitochondrial dynamics, providing a scalable and objective framework for investigating mitochondrial in vivo transport dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease models.

v6.implicacao: Ultraestrutura & Bioimagem: o desenho de validação contra anotação de especialistas serve de modelo para o grupo de trabalho de análise de dados de bioimagem do IBCCF.
v6.resumo: Arcabouço de aprendizado profundo para quantificar semiautomaticamente o transporte axonal de mitocôndrias em axônios individuais in vivo por imagem confocal time-lapse, validado contra medições de especialistas (deslocamento, velocidade e variações de intensidade e morfologia).
v6.metodo: Rastreamento por aprendizado profundo validado contra anotação manual de especialistas.

articles.titulo: Segment-dependent phylogenetic resolution reveals geographic and host sampling gaps in Oropouche virus genomes
articles.autores: Siam R, Elbehery AHA (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background. Oropouche virus (OROV) has been reported in areas beyond its historical Amazonian range since 2023, accompanied by rapid growth in publicly available genomic data. However, the extent to which these data provide reliable phylogenetic and epidemiological resolution, and whether that resolution differs among genome segments, has not been systematically examined. Methods. Nucleotide sequences annotated under Orthobunyavirus oropoucheense were retrieved from NCBI Virus (accessed 13 May 2025) and filtered to retain records at least 70% of the reference length for each segment, yielding 898 S, 831 M, and 832 L sequences. Segments were aligned independently with MAFFT, and maximum-likelihood phylogenies were inferred with IQ-TREE using ModelFinder and ultrafast bootstrap approximation. Trees were annotated with collection date, country, and host in iTOL. Results. Phylogenetic resolution differed among segments. Contemporary Brazilian sequences formed a largely unresolved region in the S segment tree, whereas the M and L trees resolved recent clusters to differing degrees. Resolution did not track segment length: the M tree resolved contemporary structure more strongly than the longer L tree, and total tree length was approximately 3.5 times greater in the M tree despite near-identical taxon sampling. Sequences collected before 2010 were recovered in supported clusters in all three segment trees, although their configuration differed by segment. These sequences were also predominantly non-Brazilian and non-human, preventing collection date, geographic origin, and host from being separated as explanations for the observed clustering. The species-level query also retained three reassortant viruses, which may influence segment-specific topologies; sequences annotated to the United States were Iquitos virus rather than OROV. Two Italian sequences clustered with Cuban sequences across all three trees, concordant with published travel histories. Conclusions. Publicly available sequences contain phylogenetic structure that differs among the S, M, and L segment trees, but interpretation is constrained by uneven temporal, geographic, and host sampling and by the inclusion of reassortant species in a species-level dataset. The concentration of sequences from Brazil and human hosts, together with limited representation of non-human hosts, restricts inference about OROV diversity and ecology. Broader and more balanced genomic surveillance would improve the ability to resolve OROV evolutionary and transmission patterns.

v6.resumo: Preprint: desde 2023 o vírus Oropouche é relatado fora da Amazônia e os genomas públicos cresceram; o trabalho avalia se esses dados dão resolução filogenética e epidemiológica confiável, e o título aponta lacunas de amostragem geográfica e de hospedeiro e resolução dependente do segmento.

articles.titulo: Tropism of Drosophila innubila Nudivirus in Cell Culture and in Tissues.
articles.autores: Mulkey KM, Schedl ME, … Unckless RL (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Most viruses are successful because they can infect and exploit specific host tissues for reproduction and transmission. As a result, we often classify viruses by their ability to infect different tissues: respiratory, reproductive and gut, for example. Thus, knowing the tissue and cellular tropism of a virus may elucidate aspects of its biology including routes of transmission and virulence. We studied tropism of the Drosophila innubila Nudivirus (DiNV) in cells and infected hosts. DiNV is a nudivirus, a family of viruses related to the baculoviruses that are relatively large (150-200 nm), contain large double-stranded DNA genomes, and infect different host tissues. Cultured cells stained with an antibody against the DiNV nucleocapsid demonstrated punctate staining in the cytoplasm by confocal microscopy. Electron micrographs of infected cells, on the other hand demonstrated that virions are present in the nucleus. After purification, DiNV was often associated with multimembrane-like vesicles as described for Oryctes rhinoceros nudivirus. We examined tropism in hosts first by sagittal section and found most virus associated with the gut and, to a lesser extent, reproductive tissues. Upon dissection and electron microscopy, we found that DiNV in the gut is primarily in the visceral muscle of the gut and not the lumen as might be expected for a virus if transmitted fecal-orally.

v6.resumo: Preprint sobre o tropismo do nudivírus de Drosophila innubila em cultura de células e em tecidos; o trecho do resumo lido trata do tecido infectado como determinante do sucesso viral (resumo lido só no início).

articles.titulo: Severe Concurrent Hypocalcemia and Hypophosphatemia Following Ferric Carboxymaltose After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: A Comparative Two-Patient Case Series.
articles.autores: Ali I, Mahgoub A, … Elhassan A (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) can cause hypophosphatemia through fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-associated renal phosphate wasting. Patients who have undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass may be particularly vulnerable because calcium and vitamin D homeostasis may already be impaired. We describe two women with previous Roux-en-Y gastric bypass who developed severe symptomatic concurrent hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia after FCM. Both had preexisting mineral vulnerability, and the findings are therefore interpreted as a multifactorial interaction rather than evidence that FCM alone caused the hypocalcemia. The first patient, aged 39 years, received FCM 500 mg weekly for five weeks (cumulative dose approximately 2,500 mg) and developed calcium 5.3 mg/dL and phosphate 0.8 mg/dL, with elevated C-terminal FGF23 and inappropriate urinary phosphate excretion during hypophosphatemia. The second patient, aged 37 years, received FCM 500 mg weekly for two doses (cumulative dose 1,000 mg) and presented approximately seven weeks later with calcium 5.9 mg/dL and a subsequent phosphate nadir of 1.3 mg/dL. Her C-terminal FGF23 was measured during early biochemical recovery and remained elevated; urinary phosphate excretion remained measurable during the hypophosphatemic/repletion period, although interpretation was limited by concurrent treatment. Both required prolonged mineral replacement, and the second patient required multiple admissions and repeated IV calcium. These cases suggest that FCM-associated phosphate disturbance may act as an additional metabolic stressor in post-bariatric patients with reduced calcium and vitamin D reserve, producing a severe combined mineral phenotype rather than isolated hypophosphatemia.

articles.titulo: Polyphosphate metabolism genes are associated with hydroxyapatite biomineralization capacity in a novel hydrogenotrophic methanogen Methanobacterium AMB_03
articles.autores: Robin-Champgneul FA, Singh A, … Neubeck A (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Methanogenic archaea play crucial roles in sedimentary phosphorus cycling, but their capacity for phosphate biomineralization remains poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that Methanobacterium AMB_03, isolated from a serpentinizing environment, mediates extracellular precipitation of carbonate-substituted hydroxyapatite (HAp) under phosphate-enriched conditions. Comparative genomic analysis of AMB_03 versus non-mineralizing strains (Methanobacterium oryzae, Methanoculleus bourgensis MAB1) shows that AMB_03 encodes polyphosphate kinase 1 (ppk1), enabling polyphosphate synthesis from ATP. In contrast, M. oryzae and MAB1 completely lack ppk1, preventing polyphosphate accumulation. Phylogenomic analysis of 320 Methanobacteriota genomes further shows that complete polyP cycling capacity is present in only ~25% of representatives, placing AMB_03 among a minority of methanogens with this capability. Experimental cultivation across phosphate gradients (0-6 mM) showed HAp early-onset precipitation was preferential at [≥]3 mM. Precipitation was eventually observed at all phosphate concentrations (except P0) by 49 weeks and was associated with extracellular polymeric substance production and localized pH increases of up to 8.08. Raman spectroscopy confirmed carbonate-substituted HAp, with characteristic peaks at 960.5 cm-1 (PO43-) and 1070-1072 cm-1 (CO32-). These findings identify a strong genomic association between polyphosphate metabolism genes and biomineralization capacity, suggesting that methanogens with complete polyP cycling systems may create localized phosphate-rich environments that promote authigenic mineral formation in sedimentary systems.

v6.implicacao: Polifosfato em osso e célula mesenquimal (colab. Danielle Bonfim) e, por afinidade, os esferitos do intestino médio de A. gemmatalis: o Raman como leitura da fase mineral associada ao polifosfato e a ligação ppk1-biomineralização são hipóteses testáveis, mas a evidência é de arqueia, em preprint, sem transferência direta a célula mesenquimal.
v6.resumo: Preprint: Methanobacterium AMB_03, arqueia metanogênica isolada de ambiente serpentinizante, precipita hidroxiapatita carbonatada fora da célula quando há fosfato. Tem ppk1 (síntese de polifosfato a partir de ATP), ausente em duas cepas que não mineralizam; entre 320 genomas de Methanobacteriota, só cerca de um quarto tem ciclo completo de polifosfato. A precipitação começou mais cedo a partir de 3 mM de fosfato, junto com substância polimérica extracelular e pH local de até 8,08 (valores conforme o registro do bioRxiv).
v6.metodo: Genômica comparativa (presença de ppk1) mais cultivo com 0 a 6 mM de fosfato e espectroscopia Raman para identificar a fase mineral (pico de fosfato perto de 960 cm-1, carbonato perto de 1070 cm-1).

articles.titulo: A replication-defective Chikungunya Virus platform for high-throughput drug screening and diagnostics.
articles.autores: Huang J, Li J, … Zhang Z (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a mosquito-borne alphavirus that poses a significant global health threat. Although vaccines have recently been approved, the requirement for Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) containment substantially impedes therapeutic and diagnostic development for CHIKV. Here, we engineered an RNA replication-defective CHIKV (CHIKV-ΔnsP4) via trans-complementation, wherein the deleted nsP4 gene product is supplied in trans. CHIKV-ΔnsP4 replicates exclusively in nsP4-expressing cells, completing a full infectious cycle, while exhibiting no detectable replication in naïve cells. Consistent with this, CHIKV-ΔnsP4 demonstrated high attenuation in animal models. Building upon this platform, we generated an mCherry-expressing RNA replication-defective reporter virus, which enabled high-content antiviral screening and serological diagnostics. Collectively, this study establishes the RNA replication-defective strategy as a safe and effective platform for CHIKV research.

v6.implicacao: Ultraestrutura & Bioimagem (CHIKV em nervos) e Imunidade & Memória Imune: infecção de ciclo único permite testar, em Aag2 que expressem nsP4, se células primadas limitam a primeira rodada de replicação.
v6.resumo: CHIKV-ΔnsP4 é um vírus com replicação defeituosa por deleção de nsP4, complementado em trans: completa o ciclo só em células que expressam nsP4, não replica em células naïve e é muito atenuado em modelos animais. A versão com mCherry permitiu triagem antiviral de alto conteúdo e sorodiagnóstico sem BSL-3.
v6.metodo: Trans-complementação de nsP4 e vírus repórter mCherry em células.

articles.titulo: Stannous Fluoride Deposition Into Plaque Biofilm: Effects of Formulation Chemistry and Hops β-Acids Extract Dispersion.
articles.revista: Compendium of continuing education in dentistry (Jamesburg, N.J. : 1995)
articles.autores: St John S, Strand R (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To evaluate how surfactant-mediated biofilm disruption by hops beta (β)-acids extract influences stannous fluoride (SnF2) penetration and interaction with extracellular metabolites, including lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
In two studies, oral biofilms were formed in vivo on artificial enamel surfaces mounted in dental appliances worn by volunteers and subsequently treated ex vivo under controlled conditions. Across the studies, biofilms were treated with supernatants of various commercial 0.454% SnF2 dentifrices containing: (1) pyrophosphate; (2) potassium nitrate (KNO3) and pyrophosphate; (3) tripolyphosphate; and (4) gluconate/citrate-stabilized 0.454% SnF2 (Crest) with and without hops β-acids extract (Activ Bio-Cleanser™). Both studies used phosphate-buffered saline as a negative control (NC). Confocal laser scanning microscopy with component-specific fluorescent probes was used to quantify Sn and LPS distribution relative to bacterial biomass, biofilm thickness, and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) structure. Image analysis was used to quantify Sn and LPS signal within bacterial regions, normalized to bacterial volume or area; statistical comparisons were made across conditions.
SnF2 uptake and penetration varied significantly across formulations. In study 1, the rank order from greatest to least for Sn deposition and LPS neutralization was: gluconate/citrate > KNO3 + pyro > pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). In study 2, the rank order from greatest to least was: gluconate/citrate + hops > gluconate/citrate > tripolyphosphate and KNO3 + pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). Some stabilized SnF2 systems exhibited limited penetration, consistent with diffusion barriers imposed by dense EPS matrices or over-stabilization reducing bioavailability. Gluconate/ citrate-stabilized SnF2-only treated biofilms showed higher deposition per unit bacteria than other SnF2 technologies but uniformly exhibited the majority of uptake in surface regions. In the formulation containing both hops and SnF2, increased Sn penetration and reduced detectable biofilm-associated LPS was observed, consistent with enhanced access of SnF2 to extracellular plaque components following surfactant-enabled biofilm modification. In this case, Sn penetration achieved high relative deposition per unit bacteria in the treated regions throughout the biofilm.
Hops β-acids extract acts as a co-surfactant in toothpaste, capable of modifying EPS structure to improve accessibility and interaction of SnF2 with extracellular metabolites within oral biofilms. The observed changes in Sn penetration and biofilm-associated, extracellular LPS are consistent with enhanced cleaning with reduced concentration of known tissue irritants.
These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for formulation strategies that enhance SnF2 accessibility within adherent oral biofilms through surfactant-based modification of EPS supporting more efficient biofilm management during oral hygiene and providing a basis for selecting toothpastes based on their efficacy.

articles.titulo: Reduced susceptibility of Cry1Ac- and Cry2Ab-resistant Helicoverpa armigera to transgenic Bt maize events and associated changes in midgut receptor gene expression.
articles.autores: Yu H, Liu B, … Liang G (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Large-scale cultivation of transgenic Bt crops effectively controls target pests but increases the risk of resistance evolution. Polyphagous pests such as Helicoverpa armigera may evolve resistance to Bt crops, and cross-resistance among Bt proteins could hasten this process. This study evaluated the susceptibility of Cry1Ac-resistant (BtR1.8, BtR3.6) and Cry2Ab-resistant (2Ab5.0, 2Ab30) H. armigera to three Bt maize events (assessed with leaf, silk, and kernel), DBN9936 (expressing Cry1Ab), DBN3601T (Cry1Ab + Vip3Aa), and Ruifeng 125 (Cry1Ab/Cry2Aj).
Compared with the susceptible 96S strain, both Cry1Ac- and Cry2Ab-resistant strains exhibited significantly reduced susceptibility to all three Bt maize events. In diet-incorporated bioassays with lyophilized leaf powder, resistance rations based on EC50 (the concentration preventing 50% of larvae from reaching the third instar within 7 days) ranged from 3.44- to 8.84-fold for Cry1Ac-resistant strains and from 2.20- to 9.53-fold for Cry2Ab-resistant strains (>12.81-fold for 2Ab30 on Ruifeng 125). Bioassays using fresh silk and kernels confirmed significantly lower mortality in resistant strains compared with 96S. Notably, pyramided events (DBN3601T and Ruifeng 125) demonstrated higher insecticidal efficacy against resistant larvae than the single-trait DBN9936, particularly in strains with lower resistance levels. Following Bt maize consumption, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) analysis revealed significant downregulation of midgut receptor genes, including ABCC2, ABCC3, ABCA2, APN1, and APN2. Specifically, ABCC2 was significantly downregulated in Cry1Ac-resistant strains, and both ABCC2 and ABCA2 were downregulated in Cry2Ab-resistant strains.
These results show that laboratory-selected Cry1Ac/Cry2Ab-resistant H. armigera have reduced susceptibility to Cry1Ab-expressing maize tissue and to the pyramided events tested. Lower transcript levels of ABCC2 and ABCA2 were associated with the resistant phenotypes, but the direct association with the reduced susceptibility was not tested. Because the strains were selected in the laboratory, these findings provide information relevant to, but cannot be directly extrapolated to, insect resistance management strategies for Bt maize in China. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

v6.implicacao: Hemócitos & homeostase intestinal (A. gemmatalis × Bt): a lista de receptores (ABCC2, ABCC3, ABCA2, APN) serve de painel de ortólogos para conferir no proteoma de intestino de A. gemmatalis exposto a Bt, mantida a ressalva de correção para múltiplos testes.
v6.resumo: Linhagens de Helicoverpa armigera resistentes a Cry1Ac e a Cry2Ab têm suscetibilidade reduzida a três eventos de milho Bt: razão de resistência de 3,44 a 8,84 vezes nas Cry1Ac e de 2,20 a 9,53 nas Cry2Ab (acima de 12,81 para 2Ab30 em Ruifeng 125). Eventos piramidados foram mais eficazes que o evento simples e, após o consumo, genes de receptores do intestino médio (ABCC2, ABCC3, ABCA2, APN1 e outros) tiveram expressão reduzida.
v6.metodo: Bioensaios com dieta de pó liofilizado de folha e com seda e grão frescos, EC50 e razão de resistência contra a linhagem suscetível 96S, e RT-qPCR de receptores do intestino médio.

articles.titulo: Widespread and diverse Wolbachia infections in sand flies from visceral leishmaniasis resurgence areas in China: potential candidates for sand fly control.
articles.autores: He YQ, Cui L, … Zhang Y (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Sand fly-borne visceral leishmaniasis (VL) has re-emerged in parts of North-central China, while conventional insecticidal control is constrained by the predominantly exophilic ecology of sand flies. Wolbachia-based approaches have shown field utility in medical vector control, but baseline data on Wolbachia infection and strain diversity in sand flies from VL resurgence settings in China remain limited.
Sand flies were collected during 2023-2024 at sentinel sites located in VL resurgence areas across four provincial-level administrative regions in China (Beijing Municipality, Shanxi Province, Henan Province, and Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region). Wolbachia was detected and typed by PCR and sequencing of the Wolbachia surface protein (wsp) gene, followed by estimation of pool positivity and bias-corrected maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)-based individual infection prevalence, haplotype inference, and phylogenetic and haplotype-network analyses.
Three sand fly species-Phlebotomus chinensis, Ph. smirnovi, and Sergentomyia squamirostris-were identified across the surveyed sites. Overall, 268 pools (10 individuals per pool; 2680 specimens) were screened for Wolbachia, and 194 pools were PCR-positive (72.4%). Bias-corrected MLE estimates indicated variable but generally high individual-level Wolbachia prevalence across Phlebotomus sampling sites, ranging from 8.6% to 100.0% in Ph. chinensis and reaching 10.4% in Ph. smirnovi, whereas Se. squamirostris was negative. WSP-based typing resolved eight haplotypes in Wolbachia from the two Phlebotomus species examined, spanning supergroups A and B; notably, Hap4 clustered with cytoplasmic incompatibility-associated Wolbachia lineages (e.g., wPip) reported in mosquitoes.
Wolbachia is highly prevalent in Phlebotomus sand flies from VL resurgence areas in North-central China and exhibits wsp-defined diversity across supergroups A and B. The detection of a wPip-related haplotype (Hap4), together with a locally prevalent Phlebotomus-associated clade, provides a baseline for prioritizing strain-level characterization and functional evaluation of Wolbachia for potential sand fly management in re-emergent VL foci.

v6.implicacao: Epidemiologia de Precisão: a estimativa por MLE a partir de pools é aplicável às coletas agrupadas de Aedes nos recortes do município.
v6.resumo: Wolbachia em flebotomíneos de áreas de reemergência de leishmaniose visceral na China: 194 de 268 pools (10 indivíduos cada) foram positivos (72,4%); a prevalência individual por máxima verossimilhança com correção de viés foi de 8,6 a 100% em Ph. chinensis e 10,4% em Ph. smirnovi, com Se. squamirostris negativa; oito haplótipos de wsp.
v6.metodo: PCR e sequenciamento de wsp em pools, estimativa de prevalência individual por MLE corrigida, redes de haplótipos.

articles.titulo: Joint species distribution modelling of insect microbiota: Time to jump onto a new opportunity.
articles.autores: Ovaskainen O, Łukasik P, … Roslin T (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: How microbes and insects influence each other is a topical question in insect science. With this contribution, we highlight joint species distribution models (JSDMs) - which model all microbial taxa in a community jointly rather than one at a time - as a statistical framework particularly well suited for resolving the drivers of host-microbe associations. While JSDM has been widely applied to microbiota of organisms other than insects, only a handful of studies have applied them thus far to insect systems. To encourage insect microbiota researchers to catch up with the benefits of JSDM, we outline the statistical and ecological basics of JSDM and give flesh to the modelling framework by reviewing how it has so far been applied to insect microbiota. We highlight the power of JSDMs in separating host, environmental and microbial drivers of community assembly, and in generating hypotheses about how different microbes influence each other. We further propose a predictive framework for identifying and characterizing five ecological categories of insect-associated microbes: (1) obligate nutritional symbionts; (2) facultative endosymbionts; (3) specialized gut associates; (4) transient microbes; and (5) pathogens and parasites. In particular, we hypothesize how the ecological characteristics of these different microbial categories are reflected in the statistical signatures recovered by JSDMs. We further suggest how JSDM can be applied to address the phylogenetic and ecological scales at which microbiome patterns are structured and to uncover how global environmental changes may reshape insect microbiota.

v6.implicacao: Hemócitos & homeostase intestinal e Imunidade & Memória Imune: JSDM para separar efeito de dieta, tratamento com Bt e colônia na microbiota intestinal.
v6.resumo: Artigo de opinião que propõe modelos conjuntos de distribuição de espécies (JSDM) para a microbiota de insetos: modelam todos os táxons juntos e separam efeitos do hospedeiro, do ambiente e das interações entre micróbios. Propõe cinco categorias ecológicas (simbiontes nutricionais obrigatórios, endossimbiontes facultativos, associados intestinais especializados, micróbios transitórios, patógenos e parasitos).
v6.metodo: Modelagem estatística conjunta de comunidades microbianas, com covariáveis de hospedeiro e ambiente.

articles.titulo: Synthetic Community Driven by a Keystone Rhizosphere Bacterium Suppresses Whitefly-Mediated Begomovirus Transmission via the Jasmonate Signaling Pathway in Tomato.
articles.autores: Zhao J, Wang Y, … Liu H (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tomato production is threatened by the combined stress of whiteflies and the whitefly-transmitted Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV). Although the rhizosphere microbiome plays a critical role in plant defense, the rational assembly strategy and underlying mechanisms of a synthetic microbial community (SynCom) targeting this insect-virus complex remain unclear. Here, leveraging the beneficial soil legacy induced by Beauveria bassiana, we constructed an eight-strain synthetic community through multi-omics analysis, soil incubation, and root exudate chemotaxis assays. One-strain knockout experiments confirmed that strain N2 is the keystone species driving the biocontrol function. Through supernatant cross-culture assays, we further refined this consortium into an optimized synthetic community (OptSynM) consisting of the single keystone strain and four helper strains. Bioassays demonstrated that OptSynM significantly reduced whitefly fitness and suppressed TYLCV accumulation in tomato plants. Within the consortium, the helper strains enhanced the rhizosphere colonization of N2 by promoting its growth and biofilm formation. Mechanistically, OptSynM activated host systemic immunity via the jasmonic acid signaling pathway. Furthermore, OptSynM maintained robust biocontrol efficacy in pot trials conducted with natural agricultural soil. Our findings highlight the practical promise of microbiome-based interventions and provide a strategic framework for using synthetic microbial communities to facilitate sustainable agricultural practices.

v6.implicacao: Hemócitos & homeostase intestinal (microbiota como terceiro elemento): desenho de nocaute de um táxon por vez como modelo para testar quais bactérias intestinais são necessárias à letalidade do Bt.
v6.resumo: Comunidade sintética de oito cepas montada a partir de omics, incubação de solo e quimiotaxia a exsudato de raiz, reduzida por nocaute de cepa única a uma cepa-chave mais quatro auxiliares (OptSynM); reduziu o fitness de mosca-branca e o acúmulo de TYLCV em tomateiro, ativando imunidade sistêmica por jasmonato.
v6.metodo: Nocaute de uma cepa por vez para achar a espécie-chave e cultivo cruzado de sobrenadantes para refinar o consórcio.

articles.titulo: Effects of Overripe Banana Processing Techniques on the Chemical Composition and Attractancy to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
articles.autores: Abuelmaali SA, Hui LW, … Abu Kassim N (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The rising incidence of vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes has become a significant public health concern. The increasing resistance of mosquitoes to conventional insecticides has prompted the need for alternative control strategies such as Attractive Targeted Sugar Baits (ATSBs). While fruit-based attractants have shown promise, the impact of different production methods on their attractiveness remains underexplored. This study investigates the effect of three production techniques of overripe banana (Musa acuminata) extracts: liquid extraction, syrup concentration, and freeze-drying, on the chemical composition and their attractiveness to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Extracts were infused into hydrogel beads and tested in dual-choice olfactometer assays to mosquito vectors Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus. Chemical profiling was conducted through Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and enzymatic sugar analysis. Results showed that all banana extracts were significantly more attractive than the 10% sucrose control. Among the extracts, syrup concentrates showed the highest attraction (PI = 0.58 {+/-} 0.17 for Ae. aegypti; 0.58 {+/-} 0.14 for Ae. albopictus), followed by freeze-dried (PI = 0.52 {+/-} 0.20; 0.54 {+/-} 0.08) and liquid extracts (PI = -0.40 {+/-} 0.04; 0.49 {+/-} 0.18). GC-MS analysis revealed that freeze-dried powder retained the greatest diversity and abundance of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), especially esters like butyl ethanoate and isoamyl acetate, which are known to influence mosquito behaviour. Although syrup concentration resulted in VOCs degradation, it also generated Maillard reaction products, such as sulphur-containing volatiles, which may enhance olfactory cues. Sugar analysis indicated that both syrup and freeze-dried extracts contained higher levels of sucrose (0.35-0.57 g/100g), glucose (21.20-28.70 g/100g), fructose (14.64-17.89 g/100g), and maltose (9.28-15.56 g/100g), aligning with mosquito preferences. Overall, the findings demonstrate that production techniques significantly influence the chemical composition and attractant potential of overripe banana extracts, offering valuable insights for the development of fruit-based mosquito lures in vector surveillance and control strategies.

articles.titulo: Terpinen-4-ol: A DEET-comparable repellent from tea tree oil with added bacteriostatic and anti-pruritic benefits.
articles.autores: Bai J, Xu X, … Fu Q (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Safe plant-derived mosquito repellents with multi-functional skin-protective properties are highly desired as alternatives to synthetic repellents. This study systematically evaluated the mosquito-repellent efficacy, electrophysiological responses, and adjunct bacteriostatic and anti-pruritic activities of terpinen-4-ol and γ-terpinene, two core constituents of Melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree) essential oil (TTO). GC-MS analysis verified that the tested TTO batch met international quality specifications, with terpinen-4-ol (35.14%) and γ-terpinene (14.90%) identified as its major volatile components. In Y-tube olfactometer assays, 10 μL terpinen-4-ol achieved 100% repellency against Aedes aegypti within 10 min. Using a WHO-aligned human arm-in-cage test, 20% terpinen-4-ol provided a mean complete protection time (CPT) of 4.75 ± 0.52 h, which was statistically comparable to 20% commercial DEET (P > 0.05). Electroantennogram recordings detected strong olfactory responses of Aedes aegypti antennae toward both monoterpenes. In-silico molecular docking targeting odorant-binding protein 1 (OBP1) from three mosquito species indicated that terpinen-4-ol could form stable complexes with OBP1, with predicted binding free energies comparable to DEET (≤ -6.61 kcal/mol). Beyond repellency, terpinen-4-ol achieved 96.39-99.66% inhibition against three common skin-pathogenic microbes (E. coli, S. aureus, C. albicans) at 24 μL/mL and alleviated dextran-40-induced pruritus in mice, whereas γ-terpinene exhibited superior ABTS radical-scavenging capacity. These findings identify terpinen-4-ol as a DEET-comparable repellent monomer with integrated benefits for preventing mosquito bites and managing bite-associated secondary infections and itching, providing a foundation for developing multi-functional natural repellent formulations.

articles.titulo: Evaluation of the bioinsecticidal potential of selected plant extracts against malaria and arboviral vectors.
articles.autores: Gebissa N, Tolossa K, … Dugassa S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Escalating environmental concerns and widespread resistance to synthetic insecticides have intensified the search for sustainable, plant-based alternatives. Botanical bioinsecticides offer a safer profile for non-target organisms and leave minimal environmental residue while effectively suppressing target vector populations.
Crude extracts from eight native medicinal plants-Ocimum lamiifolium, Lepidium sativum, Amaranthus hybridus, Premna schimperi, Ocimum gratissimum, Argemone mexicana, Lippia adoensis, and Calpurnia aurea-were prepared using 80% methanol and n-hexane solvents. Larvicidal and adulticidal bioassays were conducted under controlled laboratory conditions at concentrations ranging from 62.5 to 2000 ppm against Anopheles arabiensis, Anopheles stephensi, and Aedes aegypti. Mortality data were recorded after 24 h and evaluated via probit analysis to determine LC50 and LC90 values.
Among the tested botanicals, the non-polar n-hexane fractions exhibited significant concentration-dependent toxicity. Against Anopheles arabiensis larvae, Ocimum gratissimum displayed the highest potency (LC50 = 596.51 ppm; LC90 = 1084.48 ppm), followed closely by Argemone mexicana (LC50 = 650.88 ppm; LC90 = 1039.50 ppm). Against Aedes aegypti larvae, Lippia adoensis yielded an LC50 of 763.03 ppm (LC90 = 1158.01 ppm), while Argemone mexicana yielded an LC50 of 768.00 ppm (LC90 = 995.17 ppm). Notably, Ocimum gratissimum, Argemone mexicana, and Calpurnia aurea induced 100% larval mortality in Anopheles arabiensis at peak ceiling concentrations of 2000 ppm. Furthermore, n-hexane crude extracts of Ocimum lamiifolium, Lepidium sativum, Amaranthus hybridus, Premna schimperi, Argemone mexicana, Lippia adoensis, and Calpurnia aurea exhibited robust adulticidal efficacy against both Anopheles arabiensis and Aedes aegypti across the evaluated concentration spectrum, with Ocimum lamiifolium and Argemone mexicana achieving absolute (100%) adult mortality at 2000 ppm. All 80% methanol extracts produced negligible baseline activity and were excluded from advanced trials.
The non-polar n-hexane fractions of these local plants demonstrate promising baseline laboratory efficacy, highlighting them as candidates for further semi-field evaluation and advanced formulation testing to determine practical viability and payload durability under natural outdoor settings.
